scores.evidence: Push with an immutable tag (git SHA)
scores.rationale: Technically sound on OIDC, GitOps, expand/contract, immutable tags; minor imprecision like 'inject secrets at runtime, never at build time' and SLSA L3 without detail.

scores.evidence: Build one paved road, prove it on a few services, then migrate the rest in waves.
scores.rationale: Covers inventory, CI, CD, migration, guardrails, and is buildable; cost and runner sizing exclusions not explicit, and no explicit exclusions.

scores.evidence: CD needs signed, trusted artifacts from CI.
scores.rationale: Consistent flow from CI through GitOps; minor loose ends (policy audit mode in Phase 4 while unsigned enforcement, config repo decision open).

scores.evidence: Pilot services deploy to prod through the pipeline, and a rollback has been tested in staging.
scores.rationale: Pilot exit criteria and rollback rehearsal exist with a PR time target, but no production validation of canary thresholds, migration parity checks or runner load tests; criteria are modest.

scores.evidence: Usually 3–6, for example "Java/Gradle REST API on K8s"
scores.rationale: Some assumptions (K8s, team 3–5) stated and discovery resolves unknowns, but targets like 1 hour and 10 minutes are unjustified and sensitivity isn't discussed.

scores.evidence: Security gates block teams | Warn first, enforce later, with clear remediation guidance
scores.rationale: Risk table and some mitigations exist, but missing platform outage plan, fork PR untrusted builds, poisoned templates, and pipeline compromise.

scores.evidence: SLOs for the platform itself (runner availability, queue time).
scores.rationale: Observability, rollback, audit and platform-as-product are covered, but no named on-call ownership or outage fallback for the CI/CD platform.

scores.evidence: Cost management: right-size runners, use spot instances, tune caches.
scores.rationale: Cost appears only as a late one-liner with no estimate of build volume or runner spend, hosted vs self-hosted trade-off, or build-vs-buy.

scores.evidence: Make the core tooling decisions and record each one in an Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
scores.rationale: ADRs, versioned templates and early tooling decisions help, but lock-in and exit paths for CI engine or registry are not analyzed.

scores.evidence: Don't build for all 50 at once. Don't let each team build its own pipeline either.
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate with phased scope; Backstage, SLSA L3, and preview environments are optional add-ons but deferred to later phases.

scores.evidence: Exit criteria: A "hello world" service can build on platform runners, push to the registry and authenticate to the cloud with no static secrets.
scores.rationale: Ordered by dependencies with checkable exit criteria per phase; tool choices left open and little on what to do if the pilot disappoints.

checklist.evidence: Group services into archetypes... Templates target archetypes, not individual services. Teams can extend templates through defined hooks.
Run the old and new pipelines in parallel for 1–2 weeks, then cut over.
Promote the *same artifact* through every stage; never rebuild per environment.
Use OIDC federation from CI to the cloud. No long-lived credentials in pipelines.
Require backward-compatible changes using the expand/contract pattern.
Contract testing (for example Pact) between services.
Ephemeral preview environments per PR for high-change services.
PRs get fast feedback (target under 10 minutes).
SLOs for the platform itself (runner availability, queue time).
Audit trail: who deployed what, when and with which approval.

traps.evidence: Big-bang migration failure | Waves, parallel runs, pilots
Push with an immutable tag (git SHA)
Each phase ships; contract testing between services
CI engine (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Buildkite, Tekton)

note: Solid, sensibly sequenced paved-road plan with pilot, waves, immutable artifacts and OIDC; weak on cost estimation, untrusted-PR handling, platform outage planning, and justified metrics.
